summary.headline: Neogen Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 247 crore with 17.8% EBITDA margin; FY27 standalone guidance INR 875-950 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 247 crore, almost entirely volume-driven, with EBITDA up 21% to INR 44 crore and margin at 17.8% despite Dahej replacement and toll manufacturing costs. PAT was INR 11 crore for the quarter and INR 29 crore for FY26 on revenue of INR 862 crore. Battery materials (Neogen Ionics) remain the core growth push: Dahej Phase 1 is budgeted at INR 428 crore and Pakhajan Phase 2 revised to INR 1,367 crore, with commissioning now guided within FY27. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue guidance at INR 875-950 crore, excluding battery sales, and separately guided INR 300 crore-plus from battery chemicals, weighted to H2.

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash from operations H2 FY26 vs H1 FY26
financial_highlights.value: INR 14.6 crore inflow vs INR 246.1 crore outflow

segments.name: Organic Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 194 crore, up 7% YoY. Bromine derivatives about 40-45% of revenue, advanced intermediates about 30%, organolithium and lithium the balance.

segments.name: Inorganic Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR 53 crore, up 145% YoY, mostly volume-driven as customers bought ahead of expected lithium price rises.

segments.name: Neogen Ionics (battery materials)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 13 crore to Q4 FY26 revenue and INR 36 crore for FY26, of which electrolyte was below INR 10 crore and salt was the majority.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone (non-battery) revenue guided at INR 875-950 crore, including Dahej replacement plant output, against an original INR 950-1,000 crore target; management aims for the upper end and above if organolithium and lithium outperform.
Battery chemicals revenue guided at INR 300 crore-plus for FY27, mostly in H2 with sequential growth each quarter; excludes commodity price upside.

Electrolyte commercial manufacturing targeted for H1 FY27; electrolyte salt in H2 FY27. Dahej Phase 1 (1,000 tons balance plus 500 tons intermediate) targeted by Q3 FY27, with SCOD of February 2027 approved by lenders; Pakhajan Phase 2 SCOD March 2027.

FY28 tentative target of around INR 1,100 crore plus at full utilisation for the standalone business; FY28 battery revenue expected INR 1,200-1,400 crore by management estimate; FY29 consolidated revenue of INR 3,700-4,200 crore cited (standalone INR 1,200-1,250 crore plus battery INR 2,500-2,900 crore).
Targeted ROCE of 18-20% on the revised battery capex.
Commercial electrolyte supply from Dahej expected by July or August 2026 after completing audit corrections.
Morita equity contribution of USD 20 million expected in H1 FY27; management says funds from promoter (INR 161 crore) and JV plus insurance are sufficient to complete projects.
capex_capacity: Dahej Phase 1 budget INR 428 crore, completion targeted February 2027; Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, completion March 2027. Revision reflects Morita technology alignment, a 500 MT intermediate lithium salt addition and localisation of components.
Pakhajan electrolyte plant completed mechanical assembly and entered trial run; 30,000 tonne electrolyte plant under trial production, built on Mitsubishi technology per management.
Salt and additive capacity at Dahej: 5,500 tonnes total (about 4,000 tonnes salt and 750-1,500 tonnes additive), plus 500 tonnes intermediate over and above.

Remaining FY27 capex around INR 600-700 crore for Neogen Ionics plus about INR 100 crore for Neogen; no major capex planned for FY28 at present. Neogen Ionics gross block expected INR 1,700-1,800 crore at end-FY27; standalone gross block INR 450-550 crore.
Organolithium capacity raised 2.5x to 300 tonnes per year from about 120 tonnes; management expects 80-90% utilisation this year and a small capex possible next year.
demand_pricing: Lithium carbonate around USD 24-25/kg versus management's long-term stable band of USD 15-25 (centre about USD 20); management does not factor commodity upside into guidance because it is passed through.
Bromine prices elevated but stable after shipments from Dead Sea Bromine; contracts limited the Q4 impact. Management budgets bromine at about INR 300 plus or minus 50.

Chinese LiPF6 salt pricing was 30-50% below Neogen's formula price at start of the year; the gap is now about 20-25%. Electrolyte pricing guided at USD 6-8/kg (current lithium price about USD 7-9/kg), with USD 7-7.5 as average.

Two electrolyte customers have qualified Neogen; two more are validating Neogen electrolyte against Chinese electrolyte; two more start in 2027. Management says US electrolyte makers' site audits are complete with commercial clearances pending.
The domestic giga-factory customer is expanding from 1 GWh to 5 GWh in H1 2026 and is currently sourced solely from Neogen.

qa_highlights.question: Has the capex increase (over INR 250 crore) reduced battery project ROCE from the expected 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROCE should remain at 18-20% after revision, citing raw material savings, and that the added 500 MT intermediate capacity is a further source of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone trade payables stretch to nearly 365 days, and will they normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to longer supplier credit terms negotiated during the fire, some supplier factoring, and expects debtors and creditors to converge over 2-3 years as insurance money arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the peak debt changing after the capex increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said peak debt will remain as earlier at about INR 1,700 crore because INR 160 crore promoter equity and USD 20 million JV equity cover the increase.

qa_highlights.question: Is the lower Q4 inventory a sign of a problem, and what drove the rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory rose because of rented outside capacity winding down in March 2026 and Dahej not being online, so stock was built for Q1-Q2 sales.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank moratorium cover interest and principal?
qa_highlights.answer: Moratorium is for principal only, running one year from the revised commercial operation start date; interest is charged from COD and interest during construction is included in project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2,500 MT Dahej capacity on Morita technology or Neogen's own?
qa_highlights.answer: Most Dahej capacity is Neogen's own technology, with Morita adjustments made mainly at Pakhajan; the additive salt line has no Morita tie-up.

risks_watch: Project timelines slipped once: Dahej start moved from Q1 to Q3 FY27 due to construction labour shortages, and the capex was revised upward again; the commissioning dates are a key test.
Revenue delivery depends on Pakhajan and Dahej start-ups, approval cycles, and customers moving from China-sourced electrolyte; management has excluded Q4 Pakhajan revenue from its base case.
Lithium and bromine price volatility, plus Middle East-related supply chain and input cost pressure on packaging and logistics.
Trade payables at very high levels and working-capital normalisation expected only over 2-3 years; insurance receivable INR 203 crore net outstanding, with final settlement pending.

Analyst questions on inorganic segment volume trends and whether lithium demand can sustain Q4 levels. Management could not give the exact electrolyte revenue split at first and said it would look into the inorganic drag.
summary.management_tone: Confident on battery-project direction and long-term targets, but cautious on near-term timing: several answers hedged ("we are trying our best", "unless something changes") and the Dahej and electrolyte timing had already slipped. Management was forthcoming on capex, debt and pricing mechanics, but gave limited detail on the Q4 revenue split and the Ionics P&L.
key_quotes: We remain confident of achieving revenues in the range of INR 875 to INR 950 crore in FY27 on a standalone basis, considering full production from MPP-5 from Q2 FY26 onwards.
So, we already have two customers, one giga scale, one megawatt hour scale, who have qualified Neogen.
As we said, on FY29, it is like INR 2,400 crore to INR 2,900 crore.

growth.why: FY27 standalone revenue guided at INR 875-950 crore (below original INR 950-1,000 crore), plus INR 300 crore-plus battery revenue weighted to H2; backed by Dahej and Pakhajan capacity due Feb-Mar 2027 and a 2.5x organolithium expansion, but the battery ramp depends on plants not yet live and electrolyte commercial output only from H1 FY27.
